species.name: Mortal-Kin
species.description: Mortal-Kin are naturally born peoples whose bodies are not fundamentally defined by supernatural energy, animal physiology, undeath, or artificial construction. They vary dramatically in stature, proportions, endurance, and sensory capability. Mortal-Kin may include humans, smallfolk, giant-blooded peoples, orcish and goblinoid peoples, and other broadly mortal lineages. Spirit-bonded or psychically connected peoples may remain Mortal-Kin when that connection changes their abilities without fundamentally changing their underlying biology.

traits.name: Compact Frame
traits.text: You may move through spaces occupied by creatures at least one Size category larger than you, though you cannot end in an occupied space. You can use a passage suitable for the next smaller Size without the usual squeezing penalties, provided your body and equipment actually fit. This does not permit squeezing down several Size categories.

traits.name: Hardy
traits.text: Ordinary environmental exposure takes three times as long to affect you. The first time each Adventure an ordinary environmental hazard would cause you Damage, reduce that Damage to 0. This benefit does not apply to Damage with Breach.

traits.name: Keen
traits.text: Choose two: Low-Light Vision, Keen Hearing, or Keen Scent. Use Senses and Detection above. Within 2 units, a creature or object cannot remain Hidden from you when a chosen Sense can detect it under that Sense's stated conditions; its blockers still apply.

traits.name: Long-Limbed
traits.text: You may reach, retrieve, manipulate, or operate unattended objects up to 1 unit farther away than normal. This does not increase the Range of attacks, Reactions, Combat Cards, or other effects targeting creatures.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.text: You count as one Size category larger for lifting, carrying, pushing, dragging, and breaking ordinary objects. Double your effective carrying capacity; this does not change your occupied footprint, and multiple larger-for-hauling benefits do not repeatedly double it unless explicit. You may carry one willing or incapacitated creature without the hauling movement penalty when its body, equipment, and load fit your capacity and required support. Your hands remain occupied as needed, and terrain and other movement costs still apply.

traits.name: Stout
traits.text: Reduce involuntary movement against you by 2 units, to a minimum of 0. Ordinary wind, currents, unstable footing, and similar environmental forces must be severe before they can move or knock you down.

traits.name: Sure-Footed
traits.text: Ignore the first 2 units of Difficult Terrain you cross during each turn. You can maintain your footing on ordinary narrow, uneven, or unstable surfaces without special assistance.

traits.name: Swift
traits.text: Increase your Movement to 12 units.

traits.name: Tireless
traits.text: Ordinary travel and sustained physical labor take three times as long to cause fatigue: begin ordinary-work checks after twenty-four hours and make subsequent checks at the start of each six-hour block. The first time each Adventure fatigue or lack of rest would impose a Condition or cause Damage, ignore that consequence. This does not remove actual biological needs or change Vigor's breath-holding limit.

species.name: Feyborn
species.description: Feyborn are beings whose bodies and spirits are intertwined with glamour, dreams, emotion, living nature, shadow, and other liminal forces. They may appear nearly mortal or possess features that openly reveal their supernatural nature. Feyborn may include long-lived woodland peoples, fair folk, winged sprites, horned revelers, embodied nature spirits, dreamborn beings, changelings of fey origin, and shadow-touched peoples.

nature.name: Between Places
nature.text: You may move through spaces occupied by other creatures, though you cannot end your movement in an occupied space. Choose one Feyborn Species Trait.

traits.name: Dreamtouched
traits.text: You remain aware of your surroundings while resting. Awareness can wake you from ordinary sleep when circumstances warrant, but does not let you act while still asleep or override injury-based unconsciousness. The first time each Encounter an effect alters your perception, memory, dreams, or emotions, you immediately recognize that an outside influence is affecting you, even if you cannot identify its source or prevent the effect.

traits.name: Glamour
traits.text: After one minute of preparation, you may assume a different appearance within your general size and body plan, altering apparent lineage, age, coloration, voice, scent, clothing, and similar details. This is not Concentration. The Glamour lasts until you end it, replace it, or become unconscious. Ordinary observation cannot identify it as false, though touch, deliberate examination, or supernatural Senses may reveal inconsistencies.

traits.name: Glimmerwing
traits.text: You possess wings or another supernatural means of controlled descent. You may glide using the Gliding procedure in Combat Encounters: Movement, including normal use of Dash. This Trait does not allow you to gain height or hover.

traits.name: Greenstep
traits.text: Natural vegetation, undergrowth, mud, roots, and similar natural terrain do not count as Difficult Terrain for you. You also gain Climb 5 when climbing living plants or natural rock.

traits.name: Gloamstep
traits.text: Gain Low-Light Vision. The first time each turn you enter dim light, darkness, or substantial shadow, move 1 additional unit without spending Movement.

traits.name: Veiled Presence
traits.text: You may suppress visible and sensory signs of your supernatural nature. While suppressed, ordinary magical or spiritual detection recognizes that you are alive but does not automatically identify you as Feyborn. Direct examination or an effect specifically designed to reveal Species may still expose you.

traits.name: Wild Escape
traits.text: The first time each Encounter another creature would prevent your movement, restrain you, or reduce your Movement to 0, you may immediately move 1 unit after that effect resolves. For this move only, ignore the movement restriction created by the triggering effect. This does not ignore unrelated restrictions or permit passage through a solid barrier. The triggering effect remains afterward unless its own ending condition has been met.

species.name: Planarborn
species.description: Planarborn are peoples whose bodies are fundamentally shaped by a supernatural environment or force. That influence may be inherited, naturally occurring, or the result of a lineage transformed over generations. When selecting this Species, define an Origin with the GM that fits the Campaign. An Origin might be an elemental plane, an altered region, or another supernatural source; these are examples, not a required cosmology. Identify the specific material, energy, or environmental influence associated with it so the Species' benefits can be applied consistently. The Origin grants no benefits beyond the printed rules.

nature.name: Planar Attunement
nature.text: Ordinary environmental exposure directly associated with your Origin does not harm you. You immediately recognize significant manifestations of that Origin and can sense a concealed concentration of it within 2 units, provided it is not contained behind a sealed supernatural barrier. This does not protect you from attacks or other hostile effects. Choose one Planarborn Species Trait.

traits.name: Aegis of Origin
traits.text: Gain Resistance to one Damage type appropriate to your agreed Origin. Choose from the Damage types defined in Combat Encounters.

traits.name: Dense Form
traits.text: Reduce involuntary movement against you by 1 unit. You also count as substantially larger when lifting, carrying, pushing, or resisting ordinary environmental forces.

traits.name: Native Motion
traits.text: Gain Climb 10, Swim 10, or controlled gliding, as appropriate to your Origin. Controlled gliding follows the Gliding procedure in Combat Encounters: Movement and does not allow you to gain height or hover.

traits.name: Planar Sense
traits.text: Within 3 units, locate active portals, planar boundaries, extradimensional spaces, and significant disturbances in reality, even through ordinary visual concealment or physical barriers. A sealed supernatural barrier that blocks planar detection prevents this Sense. Identify the general kind of boundary, but not its destination, occupants, contents, or safe passage conditions.

traits.name: Resonant Step
traits.text: Terrain composed primarily of your Origin does not count as Difficult Terrain for you. The first time each turn you enter such terrain, move 1 additional unit without spending Movement.

traits.name: Shaper
traits.text: Gain the Shaper Species Combat Card under Species Combat Cards later in this chapter. It manipulates a small amount of ordinary material or energy associated with your Origin in an adjacent unoccupied space; you may maintain only one altered space at a time.

traits.name: Planar Vessel
traits.text: Once per Adventure, when you would spend the final point of one of your Resources, retain 1 point instead. Choose the affected Resource when you select this Species Trait. It should reasonably reflect your Origin.

species.name: Beastfolk
species.description: Beastfolk are sapient peoples whose defining physical qualities are drawn from animals. They may resemble mammals, birds, reptiles, insects, or combinations of several creatures. Choose an animal or related group of animals that informs your character's appearance and traits.

nature.name: Heightened Instincts
nature.text: Choose Low-Light Vision, Keen Hearing, Keen Scent, Heat Perception, Vibration Sense, or a fully defined narrow Sense appropriate to your lineage. Use Senses and Detection above. Within 2 units, creatures and objects cannot remain Hidden from you when that Sense can detect them under its stated conditions. You can follow fresh trails when the Sense can perceive the traces; this does not create traces for a Sense that cannot detect them. Choose one Beastfolk Species Trait.

traits.name: Burrower
traits.text: Gain Burrow 5 through loose soil, sand, snow, or similarly workable material. You cannot burrow through solid stone, worked flooring, or reinforced structures.

traits.name: Climber
traits.text: Gain Climb 10. When a surface can support you, you may remain secured to it without using your hands.

traits.name: Glider
traits.text: You may glide using the Gliding procedure in Combat Encounters: Movement, including normal use of Dash. This Trait does not allow you to gain height or hover.

traits.name: Natural Armament
traits.text: Choose claws, horns, fangs, a tail, mandibles, or another natural weapon. It otherwise counts as a basic one-handed weapon, does not consume Armory or Inventory capacity, and cannot be disarmed, but it uses the chosen anatomy rather than automatically requiring a free hand. Claws normally require the relevant hand or limb; horns or fangs require the head or mouth; a tail requires the tail. The required body part must be available when you attack with it. Its default Range is 1. When choosing the Trait, choose Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing Damage appropriate to its anatomy with the GM. It uses Basic Melee Attack’s normal Damage and Surge option and grants no additional equipment properties or Mounts unless another rule provides them.

traits.name: Prehensile Limb
traits.text: You possess a tail, trunk, secondary arm, or similar limb. It may hold and use one small item that can be used with one hand, other than a weapon or Guard. The item itself occupies equipment capacity normally. The limb does not grant additional Actions.

traits.name: Quadrupedal Frame
traits.text: Increase your Movement to 12 while no more than one of your hands is occupied. You also count as substantially larger when carrying riders, dragging loads, or resisting effects that would knock you down.

traits.name: Shell or Hide
traits.text: Reduce involuntary movement against you by 1 unit. The first time each Adventure an ordinary environmental hazard would cause you Damage, reduce that Damage to 0. This benefit does not apply to Damage with Breach.

traits.name: Swimmer
traits.text: Gain Swim 10. This changes your movement through water; it does not grant underwater breathing.

species.name: Dragonkin
species.description: Dragonkin are peoples descended from dragons, created in their image, or fundamentally shaped by draconic power. Although they may possess reptilian or serpentine features, their supernatural lineage distinguishes them from ordinary Beastfolk. Define a Draconic Lineage with the GM that fits the Campaign, identifying the specific power or environmental affinity expressed by your lineage.

nature.name: Draconic Core
nature.text: Ordinary environmental exposure associated with your Draconic Lineage does not harm you. You may also project a brief harmless manifestation of your Lineage up to 1 unit away, allowing you to ignite or extinguish tinder, chill or warm a small object, scatter loose material, produce light, create a sharp sound, or cause another comparable environmental effect. Choose one Dragonkin Species Trait.

traits.name: Burrowing Claws
traits.text: Gain Burrow 5 through loose earth, sand, snow, or similarly workable material.

traits.name: Draconic Armament
traits.text: Choose claws, horns, fangs, or a tail as a natural weapon. It otherwise counts as a basic one-handed weapon, does not consume Armory or Inventory capacity, and cannot be disarmed, but it uses the chosen anatomy rather than automatically requiring a free hand. Claws normally require the relevant hand or limb; horns or fangs require the head or mouth; a tail requires the tail. The required body part must be available when you attack with it. Its default Range is 1. When choosing the Trait, choose Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing Damage appropriate to its anatomy with the GM. It uses Basic Melee Attack’s normal Damage and Surge option and grants no additional equipment properties or Mounts unless another rule provides them.

traits.name: Hoard Sense
traits.text: After handling an object for one minute, you may claim it as part of your hoard. While it remains within the same region, you know its general direction and whether it is moving. You may have only one claimed object at a time. You can also identify an examined object's primary material, general quality, and whether it is an obvious imitation.

traits.name: Lineage Scales
traits.text: The first time each Encounter you take Damage from a source directly associated with your Draconic Lineage, reduce that Damage by 1. This protection does not prevent Breach.

traits.name: Tail Balance
traits.text: Ignore the first unit of Difficult Terrain you cross each turn and reduce involuntary movement against you by 1 unit.

traits.name: True Breath
traits.text: Gain the True Breath Species Combat Card under Species Combat Cards later in this chapter. Once per Encounter, it releases your Draconic Lineage in a 2-unit cone to change terrain, clear loose material, or create visual obstruction. It does not directly cause Damage.

traits.name: Wings
traits.text: You may glide using the Gliding procedure in Combat Encounters: Movement, including normal use of Dash. This Trait does not allow you to gain height or hover.

species.name: Tideborn
species.description: Tideborn are aquatic and amphibious peoples whose bodies are adapted to oceans, rivers, swamps, reefs, flooded caverns, and other submerged environments. Tideborn may resemble fish, amphibians, marine mammals, cephalopods, crustaceans, aquatic reptiles, or beings with no terrestrial equivalent.

nature.name: Amphibious Body
nature.text: Gain Swim 10. You can breathe both air and water and function normally while submerged. Ordinary water pressure, currents, and temperature within habitable depths do not impair you. Choose one Tideborn Species Trait.

traits.name: Adhesive Limbs
traits.text: Gain Climb 10 through suckers, gripping pads, hooked limbs, or a similar adaptation. You may remain secured to a surface without using your hands.

traits.name: Bioluminescence
traits.text: During your Turn, you may begin or suppress your bodily light without an Action. It provides clear light within 1 unit and dim light out to 2 units. To leave a luminous mark on an adjacent creature or object during Combat, use Perform Task and burn its normal 2 Action dice. An unattended object or willing creature needs no roll. Against an unwilling creature, roll Grace + an applicable Non-Combat Skill against its Fortitude. Use Grace + 5 for a directly applicable Key Aspect, or Grace alone if no Skill applies. This specific use of Perform Task is non-damaging, produces no Surges, and permits legal Reactions before resolution. On success, the mark lasts until the Encounter ends or someone within reach uses Perform Task to remove it. Ordinary darkness cannot conceal the marked subject, but cover, opaque barriers, and other concealment still can.

traits.name: Echolocation
traits.text: Within 3 units, you can emit and hear brief echoes to pinpoint exposed shapes and movement despite visual darkness, smoke, or similar visual concealment. Echolocation reveals no color, writing, or fine visual detail. It requires a continuous air or water path carrying sound to the subject and back; solid barriers and effects preventing emission or hearing block it. The emitted sound can itself be heard. It functions passively and costs no dice.

traits.name: Electric Sense
traits.text: While submerged, detect the presence and approximate direction and distance of living creatures within 3 units through the electrical activity of their bodies. You and the subject must share a continuous body of water; a sealed barrier or an effect blocking electrical sensing prevents detection. Visual concealment does not interfere. This Sense does not reveal identity, condition, or an exact occupied space for targeting; use another Sense or a deliberate search to locate the creature precisely.

traits.name: Flexible Body
traits.text: You may pass through openings your flexible body and equipment can actually fit through, bypassing the usual one-Size squeezing limit. Apply the normal squeezing Movement cost and −1 Fortitude. You may move through creatures’ spaces but cannot end in a space still occupied by a conscious creature, or pass through sealed barriers.

traits.name: Ink Cloud
traits.text: Gain the Ink Cloud Species Combat Card under Species Combat Cards later in this chapter. Once per Encounter while submerged, it creates one adjacent hex of opaque ink that blocks ordinary sight.

traits.name: Jet Propulsion
traits.text: Increase your Swim Movement to 12. The first time you Dash while swimming during each turn, move 1 additional unit.

species.name: Verdant
species.description: Verdant characters are living plants, fungal colonies, coral-like organisms, animated wood, or other beings whose bodies grow rather than develop as ordinary flesh. Some are individual organisms, while others are colonies functioning as a single conscious being.

nature.name: Rooted Life
nature.text: You do not require conventional food. Choose an appropriate source of nourishment, such as sunlight, water, minerals, decay, or organic matter. At the end of your Turn, you may become Rooted while in contact with a stable surface. While Rooted, your Movement is 0; you cannot voluntarily leave your space or gain voluntary extra Movement, including through Dash or other granted movement, unless an effect explicitly bypasses being Rooted. Involuntary movement against you is reduced by 2 units, to a minimum of 0. You may cease being Rooted at the start of your Turn. Choose one Verdant Species Trait.

traits.name: Blooming
traits.text: At the beginning of each Adventure, produce one simple piece of organic Temporary Equipment equivalent to ordinary Tier 1 non-combat equipment. It may be food, medicine ingredients, resin, fiber, dye, a light-producing growth, or a similar nonweapon item. It decays or becomes unusable at the end of the Adventure.

traits.name: Barked Form
traits.text: While Rooted, increase your Resilience by 1. This bonus ends immediately when you cease being Rooted.

traits.name: Mycelial Sense
traits.text: While touching natural soil, connected roots, or fungal growth, detect movement within 3 units transmitted through that continuous natural surface. You learn approximate direction and distance, not an exact occupied space for targeting. Visual concealment does not interfere. Airborne or motionless creatures, a break in the natural connection, and worked flooring that separates a creature from it prevent detection. Use another Sense or a deliberate search to locate a detected creature precisely.

traits.name: Photosynthetic Reserve
traits.text: Once per Adventure, after spending at least ten minutes in contact with your chosen source of nourishment, recover 1 point of one Resource.

traits.name: Regrowth
traits.text: The first time each Adventure a Wound Condition or other effect would disable one of your limbs or Senses, that limb or Sense remains functional for one minute (six Rounds). Minor lost body parts regrow during appropriate recovery.

traits.name: Spore Cloud
traits.text: Gain the Spore Cloud Species Combat Card under Species Combat Cards later in this chapter. Once per Encounter, it creates one adjacent hex of spores, pollen, or drifting growth that blocks ordinary sight.

traits.name: Symbiotic Growth
traits.text: You possess an additional vine, tendril, branch, or symbiotic organism. It may hold and use one small item that can be used with one hand, other than a weapon or Guard. The item itself occupies equipment capacity normally. The growth does not grant additional Actions.

traits.name: Vine-Limbed
traits.text: Gain Climb 10. You may remain secured to a suitable surface without using your hands.

species.name: Deathless
species.description: Deathless characters continue to exist after ordinary biological life has ended or are sustained in a condition between life and death. Their continued existence may depend upon necromancy, spiritual force, hunger, memory, shadow, unfinished purpose, or another extraordinary condition.

nature.name: Deathless Nature
nature.text: You do not need to breathe or eat and do not sleep in the ordinary manner. Ordinary biological diseases and poisons do not affect you, though you must still rest and recover normally. Deathless Nature - Playtest: your Death Track ends at 7 instead of 5. When all five Core Wound spaces first fill, become Dying at 0/7; reaching 7 causes death. Advancement of the Death Track, exertion while Dying, additional Wounds, Stabilization, retained progress, and recovery otherwise follow the normal rules. Your Core Wound track still has five spaces. Choose one Deathless Species Trait.

traits.name: Borrowed Life
traits.text: After one minute of preparation, you may imitate warmth, breathing, coloration, a heartbeat, and similar signs of life. This is not Concentration. The effect lasts until you end it, replace it, or become unconscious. Ordinary observation cannot identify you as Deathless; medical or supernatural examination may reveal your nature.

traits.name: Detached Scout
traits.text: Use Perform Task to detach or reattach one small sensory part within reach, burning its normal 2 Action dice in Combat. Choose one ordinary Sense to perceive through the part. Within 5 units, you receive that Sense from the part's position with its normal limitations. Your main body loses the corresponding Sense or function while the part is detached. The part cannot move or act and grants no extra Actions. Perception costs no further dice. It stops if the part is destroyed or moves beyond 5 units, and resumes if the intact part returns within range. Reattachment restores the body's function. If the part is destroyed, appropriate care during a Recovery restores both the part and its function.

traits.name: Grave Sense
traits.text: Within 3 units, pinpoint creatures and remains and distinguish living, dead, Deathless, and artificially animated subjects. Ordinary visual concealment does not block this Sense; a sealed barrier or an effect explicitly masking this detection does. It does not reveal identity, thoughts, cause of death, or concealed abilities. Empty objects without life, remains, or animation do not register.

traits.name: Shadowed Soul
traits.text: The first time each turn you enter dim light or darkness, move 1 additional unit without spending Movement.

traits.name: Spectral Flexibility
traits.text: You may pass through openings your spectral body and equipment can actually fit through, bypassing the usual one-Size squeezing limit. Apply the normal squeezing Movement cost and −1 Fortitude. You may move through creatures’ spaces but cannot end in a space still occupied by a conscious creature, or pass through solid walls or sealed barriers.

traits.name: Stitched Form
traits.text: You possess an additional arm, skeletal limb, tendril, or other appendage. It may hold and use one small item that can be used with one hand, other than a weapon or Guard. The item itself occupies equipment capacity normally. The limb does not grant additional Actions.

traits.name: Uncanny Stillness
traits.text: You can remain motionless indefinitely and display no involuntary signs of life. While Hidden and motionless, ordinary visual observation does not reveal you unless someone performs a deliberate search.

traits.name: Unyielding Remains
traits.text: The first time each Adventure a Wound Condition would reduce your Movement, disable a limb, or impair one of your Senses, ignore that portion of the Condition for one minute (six Rounds).

species.name: Constructs
species.description: Constructs are artificial peoples created through machinery, magic, alchemy, craftsmanship, or some combination of those methods. Their bodies may be made from metal, stone, wood, ceramic, crystal, synthetic flesh, or other designed materials.

nature.name: Artificial Nature
nature.text: You do not need to breathe or eat and do not sleep in the ordinary manner. Ordinary biological diseases and poisons do not affect you, though you must still rest and recover normally. Choose one Construct Species Trait. You may replace your chosen Species Trait during significant Downtime, representing modification or reconstruction of your body.

traits.name: Alternate Chassis
traits.text: Gain Climb 10 or Swim 10 through a body specifically designed for that form of Movement.

traits.name: Anchor Mode
traits.text: At the end of your Turn, you may anchor yourself to a stable surface. While anchored, your Movement is 0; you cannot voluntarily leave your space or gain voluntary extra Movement, including through Dash or other granted movement, unless an effect explicitly bypasses the anchor. Involuntary movement against you is reduced to 0. You may release the anchor at the start of your Turn.

traits.name: Integrated Tool
traits.text: Choose one ordinary Non-Combat Toolkit and incorporate it into your body. It does not consume Armory or Inventory capacity, cannot be disarmed, and remains available whenever the relevant portions of your body are functional.

traits.name: Internal Compartment
traits.text: Choose one small item of ordinary utility equipment within the Team's ordinary access. While installed inside your body, it does not consume Armory or Inventory capacity and is not discovered through casual observation. You may replace it during significant Downtime.

traits.name: Redundant Systems
traits.text: The first time each Adventure a Wound Condition or other effect would disable one of your limbs, Senses, or Movement modes, that function remains available for one minute (six Rounds).

traits.name: Reinforced Frame
traits.text: Reduce involuntary movement against you by 1 unit. If you have not moved during the current turn, reduce it by 2 units instead.

traits.name: Sensor Suite
traits.text: Choose two: Low-Light Vision, Keen Hearing, Heat Perception, Vibration Sense, or a fully defined narrow Sense appropriate to the Campaign. Use Senses and Detection above. Within 2 units, creatures and objects cannot remain Hidden from you when a chosen Sense can detect them under its stated conditions; its blockers still apply.

traits.name: Utility Limb
traits.text: You possess an additional arm, tool mount, cable, or similar mechanism. It may hold and use one small item that can be used with one hand, other than a weapon or Guard. The item itself occupies equipment capacity normally. The limb does not grant additional Actions.

heritages.name: Warcamp Raised
heritages.description: You were raised among soldiers, camp followers, quartermasters, healers, and the families that traveled with an army or lived around a permanent garrison.

legacy.name: Quartermaster's Due
legacy.text: During Character Creation, gain one Chassis and one compatible Fitting, each up to 1 Tier above the Team's normal procurement Tier, to a maximum of Tier 5. In a Tier 1 Team, you can choose a Tier 2 Chassis and Tier 2 Fitting. The assembled item occupies Armory and Inventory capacity normally.

familiarity.name: Camp Discipline
familiarity.text: You recognize common military ranks, unit markings, signals, supply arrangements, watch rotations, and camp layouts. You know how to move through an organized military position without disrupting its operations and how to approach the appropriate person when requesting supplies, information, or an audience. This grants no military rank or authority.

heritages.name: Merchant Family
heritages.description: You were raised around shops, caravans, counting houses, warehouses, or family ventures in which every possession had a cost and every relationship had practical value.

legacy.name: Family Ledger
legacy.text: At the beginning of each Adventure, gain 1 Temporary Influence. Temporary Influence granted by this Legacy that remains when the Adventure ends is lost.

familiarity.name: Commercial Networks
familiarity.text: You recognize guild marks, shipping labels, trade conventions, common commercial deceptions, and signs of shortage or surplus. In a settlement with an established market, you can identify the brokers, wholesalers, guild representatives, and other people through whom serious business is conducted.

heritages.name: Noble Household
heritages.description: You were born or raised within a titled family, political dynasty, landed household, or another lineage whose name carries recognized social weight.

legacy.name: Letters of Standing
legacy.text: You may invoke your family name when dealing with an established institution such as a merchant guild, government office, temple, academy, or military command. For the current Encounter, treat your Reach as 1 higher and gain 1 Temporary Influence that can only be used during that Encounter. The first use each Adventure is free. Each additional use creates 1 ordinary Influence pressure.

familiarity.name: Unspoken Precedence
familiarity.text: You understand formal etiquette, inheritance, favors, veiled insults, and the difference between official title and practical authority. In elite gatherings, you can recognize who holds informal influence and when an apparently polite gesture carries political meaning.

heritages.name: Artisan Household
heritages.description: You grew up in a smithy, workshop, mill, studio, construction yard, or another household centered on skilled production.

legacy.name: Inherited Tools
legacy.text: Choose one ordinary Toolkit during Character Creation. It does not consume Armory capacity and may be included in your Inventory without consuming Inventory capacity. You may replace it at the end of an Adventure or during suitable Downtime.

familiarity.name: Workshop Rhythm
familiarity.text: You recognize common materials, construction methods, maker's marks, rushed workmanship, and obvious substitutions. You understand workshop hierarchy and can approach laborers, apprentices, and craftspeople without behaving like an intrusive outsider.

heritages.name: Academy Raised
heritages.description: You were raised among tutors, books, archives, laboratories, or institutions devoted to formal study and the preservation of knowledge.

legacy.name: Formal Education
legacy.text: Gain 1 additional Non-Combat Skill Point during Character Creation. This point cannot raise a Skill above the normal starting limit.

familiarity.name: Institutional Literacy
familiarity.text: You understand academic organization, citation, archival procedure, and the politics of formal scholarship. You can recognize obvious censorship, deliberate omissions, and records written primarily to satisfy institutional expectations. You also know how to identify the appropriate archive, specialist, department, or institution to approach when seeking information.

heritages.name: Temple Raised
heritages.description: You were raised within a temple, monastery, shrine, religious family, or institution whose doctrine and observances shaped daily life.

legacy.name: Sacred Trust
legacy.text: The first time each Adventure ordinary Influence pressure would pass through your Reach and remove Temporary Influence or mark Core Influence, reduce that pressure by 1. This protection does not prevent Influence Breach.

familiarity.name: Sacred Practice
familiarity.text: You recognize common symbols, rituals, offices, doctrinal divisions, and forms of address used by established religious institutions. You can identify when a public observance differs from accepted practice, though you do not automatically know the reason.

heritages.name: Underworld Raised
heritages.description: You grew up among crowded streets, informal shelters, smugglers, thieves, fences, and people who survived outside official systems. You learned where goods disappear, who moves them, and which rules matter when the law offers no protection.

legacy.name: Fence's Cache
legacy.text: At the end of an Adventure, you may preserve one piece of Temporary Equipment as your Cached Item. It remains usable Temporary Equipment across Adventures and counts against neither Armory nor Inventory capacity while cached. This Legacy preserves the item’s actual condition and remaining Uses; it does not repair or replenish it. You may keep only one Cached Item. With access to a black market, fence, or appropriate illicit organization, you may exchange it for Temporary Equipment of comparable or lower access that the Team's Tier and actual connections could reasonably obtain. The replacement becomes your Cached Item. If you replace a cached item without exchanging it, or stop preserving it, resolve the former item normally: admit it to your Armory within capacity, sell, trade, return, or discard it.

familiarity.name: Quiet Rules
familiarity.text: You recognize territorial signs, protection arrangements, false storefronts, informal shelters, hidden markets, secondary routes, and the people who actually control illicit trade. You know how to locate a discreet intermediary, safe meeting place, or overlooked refuge without immediately presenting yourself as an obvious victim or agent of authority.

heritages.name: Caravan Family
heritages.description: You were raised among traders, performers, pilgrims, nomads, couriers, or traveling families for whom roads and temporary camps were home. Constant exposure to unfamiliar places taught you how to pick up new practices quickly.

legacy.name: Lessons of the Road
legacy.text: At the beginning of each Adventure, choose one Non-Combat Skill you do not possess. Treat that Skill as Rank 1 until the Adventure ends.

familiarity.name: Road Lore
familiarity.text: You recognize traveler marks, route warnings, regional accents, common road hazards, and signs that a path is less safe than it appears. In an unfamiliar settlement, you can quickly locate places where outsiders arrange passage, seek work, exchange news, and trade informal favors.

heritages.name: Frontier Household
heritages.description: You grew up in an isolated settlement, border territory, remote colony, or community that could not depend upon immediate aid from outside.

legacy.name: Prepared Cache
legacy.text: You may reveal that you previously packed, purchased, or concealed one ordinary non-combat item appropriate to the current environment. It must be something your character could reasonably obtain through the Team's ordinary access and the character's actual circumstances and cannot be a Weapon, Armor, Guard, Implement, Consumable Kit, or other significant Combat equipment. The item becomes Temporary Equipment. The first use each Adventure is free. Each additional use creates 1 ordinary Influence pressure.

familiarity.name: Borderland Vigilance
familiarity.text: You recognize how isolated communities organize alarms, food stores, shelters, escape routes, and defensive positions. You can identify practical vulnerabilities and signs that a community expects attack, shortage, or abandonment.

distinctions.name: Athlete
distinctions.description: Athletes are combatants who have pushed their physical capabilities through discipline, experience, or relentless conditioning. They may be brawlers, duelists, soldiers, martial artists, bodyguards, or any other characters whose Combat identity begins with what their bodies can accomplish.
distinctions.benefit: Gain one additional Prowess Expertise and two additional Prowess Combat Cards. If this Distinction is acquired later, instead increase Prowess to a minimum of Rank 2, then gain one additional Prowess Expertise and four additional Prowess Combat Cards.

origin.name: Peak Performance
origin.text: Increase your Resilience by 1. During your first Turn of an Encounter, double your normal Movement allowance. Apply ordinary terrain costs and movement restrictions. Extra Movement granted by Dash, burned dice, or another ability is not doubled. If you have several movement modes, this doubles their normal allowances without granting additional separate movement budgets.

distinctions.name: Marksman
distinctions.description: Marksmen project force accurately across the battlefield. They may be archers, snipers, gunslingers, siege specialists, or other combatants who rely on distance, precision, and deliberate target selection.
distinctions.benefit: Gain one additional Ballistics Expertise and two additional Ballistics Combat Cards. If this Distinction is acquired later, instead increase Ballistics to a minimum of Rank 2, then gain one additional Ballistics Expertise and four additional Ballistics Combat Cards.

origin.name: Split Focus
origin.text: You may maintain two Locks at once. If you would establish Lock on a third creature, choose which existing Lock ends.

distinctions.name: Gifted
distinctions.description: The Gifted possess capabilities that are part of what they are rather than something learned entirely through study or ritual. They reshape themselves to meet changing problems, altering their bodies to fill whatever role is most useful in the moment.
distinctions.benefit: Gain access to the Gestalt Combat Style. If this Distinction is acquired later, gain access to Gestalt, increase it to Rank 2, then gain one additional Gestalt Expertise and two additional Gestalt Combat Cards.

origin.name: Efficient Transformation
origin.text: Reduce the Stamina upkeep of your maintained Adaptation by 1, to a minimum of 0. This does not reduce the initial cost of assuming an Adaptation. The additional upkeep caused by Unstable is not reduced by this benefit.

distinctions.name: Strategist
distinctions.description: Strategists are problem-solvers, infiltrators, engineers, field medics, tacticians, and manipulators who win by understanding what is likely to happen before it occurs. Their advantage comes from preparing responses, limiting enemy choices, and turning predictable behavior into exploitable openings.
distinctions.benefit: Gain one additional Cunning Expertise and two additional Cunning Combat Cards. If this Distinction is acquired later, instead increase Cunning to a minimum of Rank 2, then gain one additional Cunning Expertise and four additional Cunning Combat Cards.

origin.name: Branching Plans
origin.text: You may establish a second Contingency each round. You may still trigger only one Contingency per round unless another rule says otherwise.

distinctions.name: Psyker
distinctions.description: Psykers possess minds that operate beyond ordinary limits. Their abilities may manifest as telekinetic force, mental influence, expanded perception, projected thought, bodily control, or other expressions of focused consciousness.
distinctions.benefit: Gain access to the Psionics Combat Style. If this Distinction is acquired later, gain access to Psionics, increase it to Rank 2, then gain one additional Psionics Expertise and two additional Psionics Combat Cards.

origin.name: Sacrificial Power
origin.text: When using a Psionics Action or Reaction, first pay its full minimum primary commitment from the appropriate Pool, never fewer than 2 Pool dice. A minimum-3 card still consumes at least 3 Pool dice. After that payment, you may spend Temporary Wounds instead of additional dice. Each Temporary Wound replacing an additional rolled die supplies one normal d10, subject to the card's usual roll maximum. Each Temporary Wound replacing an additional burned die pays that secondary cost without a roll. These substitutions do not waive any other requirements or costs.

distinctions.name: Arcanist
distinctions.description: Arcanists approach supernatural power as something that can be studied, constructed, and refined. Their Actions shape magical forces and create Threads that interact with later spellwork.
distinctions.benefit: Gain access to the Magecraft Combat Style. If this Distinction is acquired later, gain access to Magecraft, increase it to Rank 2, then gain one additional Magecraft Expertise and two additional Magecraft Combat Cards.

origin.name: Elemental Versatility
origin.text: The first time you use an Action Card of a particular Magecraft subtype during an Encounter, gain one additional Surge for that Action.

distinctions.name: Orator
distinctions.description: Orators are battlefield commanders, officers, champions, performers, and leaders whose presence changes how others fight. They issue orders, provoke enemies, raise standards, protect allies, and lead through personal action. Orators are rarely removed from the fighting. They place themselves where their direction and example have the greatest effect.
distinctions.benefit: Gain one additional Leadership Expertise and two additional Leadership Combat Cards. If this Distinction is acquired later, instead increase Leadership to a minimum of Rank 2, then gain one additional Leadership Expertise and four additional Leadership Combat Cards.

origin.name: Commanding Authority
origin.text: Each occupied Leadership card can hold up to two Authority results. After resolving a Leadership Action, you may store up to two results from separate dice actually rolled for it on that Action's card. Keep or individually replace existing results, without exceeding two. Each rolled die supplies at most one stored result. The card occupies one Authority capacity slot. Spending one result leaves the other available, and neither can be transferred to another card. You still cannot substitute more than one Authority result per Action or Reaction.

distinctions.name: Invoker
distinctions.description: Invokers prepare supernatural effects that bind power into creatures, objects, locations, and declared conditions. In Combat, they establish Wards, Hexes, Divinations, Imbuements, Offerings, and other Rites, then exploit the moments when those Rites are fulfilled. Their strength comes from preparation, prediction, and maintaining the right combination of effects as the Encounter changes.
distinctions.benefit: Gain access to the Ritualism Combat Style. If this Distinction is acquired later, gain access to Ritualism, increase it to Rank 2, then gain one additional Ritualism Expertise and two additional Ritualism Combat Cards.

origin.name: Final Echo
origin.text: You may maintain one additional Rite. Once per round, when you remove one of your Rites to establish another, you may resolve the removed Rite's Echo once before removing it. Ignore its Trigger and choose any valid target or area.

distinctions.name: Summoner
distinctions.description: Summoners are conduits who forge bonds with extraordinary entities, forces, or powers whose nature and origin are established by the Campaign. They channel portions of those bonds through Calling Actions and may eventually allow a manifestation to fully enter the battlefield.
distinctions.benefit: Gain access to the Calling Combat Style. If this Distinction is acquired later, gain access to Calling, increase it to Rank 2, then gain one additional Calling Expertise and two additional Calling Combat Cards.

origin.name: Greater Manifestation
origin.text: Reduce the additional burned-die cost of Full Manifestation by 1, to a minimum of 0. This does not reduce the normal dice commitment of the Calling Combat Card used to enter Full Manifestation.
